unit.why: A short anecdote: a woman whose children kept dying brings her small daughter to the Maggid, who blesses the girl, and the blessing is fulfilled.

stories.start_quote: עוד שם בחארזיל הי' ר׳ שמואל משה גוטליב
stories.summary_en: Pessel, wife of R. Shmuel Moshe Gottlieb of Chorzele, whose children kept dying, brings her two-year-old daughter Frumet to the Maggid. He takes the child's hand and promises she will have a minyan of children, which comes true; Frumet later becomes mother-in-law of the Serock rabbi, whose family prospers.

tags.why: The story turns on the Maggid's promise and its fulfilment.
His prediction of ten descendants comes true.

quotes: ונסעה אשתו מ' פעסל עם בתה הילדה
tags.why: The mother travels to the Maggid with her request.
The tzaddik's blessing and touch are what secure the child's future.

tags.why: The daughter Frumet is the object of the blessing and its later fulfilment.
